# Operational Best Practices for

Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (CCCS) Medium Cloud Control Profile

Conformance packs provide a general-purpose compliance framework designed to enable you to
create security, operational or cost-optimization governance checks using managed or custom
AWS Config rules and AWS Config remediation actions. Conformance Packs, as sample templates, are not
designed to fully ensure compliance with a specific governance or compliance standard. You
are responsible for making your own assessment of whether your use of the Services meets
applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

The following provides a sample mapping between the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security
(CCCS) Medium Cloud Control Profile and AWS managed Config rules. Each Config rule applies
to a specific AWS resource, and relates to one or more CCCS Medium Cloud Control Profile
controls. A CCCS Medium Cloud Control Profile control can be related to multiple Config
rules. Refer to the table below for more detail and guidance related to these mappings.

| Control ID          | Control Description                                                            | AWS Config Rule                                                                                                                                                                    | Guidance                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

| | CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.A   | AC-2.A Account Management                                                      | [iam-policy-no-statements-with-full-access](iam-policy-no-statements-with-full-access.md "iam-policy-no-statements-with-full-access.md")                                           | Ensure IAM Actions are restricted to only those actions<br>that are needed. Allowing users to have more privileges than needed to<br>complete a task may violate the principle of least privilege and separation<br>of duties.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.A   | AC-2.A Account Management                                                      | [iam-root-access-key-check](iam-root-access-key-check.md "iam-root-access-key-check.md")                                                                                           | Access to systems and assets can be controlled by checking<br>that the root user does not have access keys attached to their AWS Identity<br>and Access Management (IAM) role. Ensure that the root access keys are<br>deleted. Instead, create and use role-based AWS accounts to help to<br>incorporate the principle of least functionality.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.A   | AC-2.A Account Management                                                      | [iam-user-group-membership-check](iam-user-group-membership-check.md "iam-user-group-membership-check.md")                                                                         | AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you<br>restrict access permissions and authorizations, by ensuring users are<br>members of at least one group. Allowing users more privileges than needed to<br>complete a task may violate the principle of least privilege and separation<br>of duties.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.A   | AC-2.A Account Management                                                      | [iam-user-no-policies-check](iam-user-no-policies-check.md "iam-user-no-policies-check.md")                                                                                        | This rule ensures AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)<br>policies are attached only to groups or roles to control access to systems<br>and assets. Assigning privileges at the group or the role level helps to<br>reduce opportunity for an identity to receive or retain excessive<br>privileges.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.A   | AC-2.A Account Management                                                      | [iam-user-unused-credentials-check](iam-user-unused-credentials-check.md "iam-user-unused-credentials-check.md")                                                                   | AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you with<br>access permissions and authorizations by checking for IAM passwords and<br>access keys that are not used for a specified time period. If these unused<br>credentials are identified, you should disable and/or remove the<br>credentials, as this may violate the principle of least privilege. This rule<br>requires you to set a value to the maxCredentialUsageAge (Config Default:<br>90). The actual value should reflect your organization's policies.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.A   | AC-2.A Account Management                                                      | [multi-region-cloudtrail-enabled](multi-region-cloudtrail-enabled.md "multi-region-cloudtrail-enabled.md")                                                                         | AWS CloudTrail records AWS Management Console actions and<br>API calls. You can identify which users and accounts called AWS, the source<br>IP address from where the calls were made, and when the calls occurred.<br>CloudTrail will deliver log files from all AWS Regions to your S3 bucket if<br>MULTI_REGION_CLOUD_TRAIL_ENABLED is enabled. Additionally, when AWS launches<br>a new Region, CloudTrail will create the same trail in the new Region. As a<br>result, you will receive log files containing API activity for the new<br>Region without taking any action.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.B   | AC-2.B Account Management                                                      | [cloudtrail-enabled](cloudtrail-enabled.md "cloudtrail-enabled.md")                                                                                                                | AWS CloudTrail can help in non-repudiation by recording<br>AWS Management Console actions and API calls. You can identify the users and<br>AWS accounts that called an AWS service, the source IP address where the<br>calls generated, and the timings of the calls. Details of captured data are<br>seen within AWS CloudTrail Record Contents.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.B   | AC-2.B Account Management                                                      | [ec2-imdsv2-check](ec2-imdsv2-check.md "ec2-imdsv2-check.md")                                                                                                                      | Ensure the Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2)<br>method is enabled to help protect access and control of Amazon Elastic<br>Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance metadata. The IMDSv2 method uses<br>session-based controls. With IMDSv2, controls can be implemented to restrict<br>changes to instance metadata.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |

This control<br>checks for unexpected privilege escalation when a task definition has host<br>networking enabled but the customer has not opted-in to elevated<br>privileges.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.B   | AC-2.B Account Management                                                      | [emr-kerberos-enabled](emr-kerberos-enabled.md "emr-kerberos-enabled.md")                                                                                                          | The access permissions and authorizations can be managed<br>and incorporated with the principles of least privilege and separation of<br>duties, by enabling Kerberos for Amazon EMR clusters. In Kerberos, the<br>services and the users that need to authenticate are known as principals.<br>The principals exist within a Kerberos realm. Within the realm, a Kerberos<br>server is known as the key distribution center (KDC). It provides a means<br>for the principals to authenticate. The KDC authenticates by issuing tickets<br>for authentication. The KDC maintains a database of the principals within<br>its realm, their passwords, and other administrative information about each<br>principal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.B   | AC-2.B Account Management                                                      | [iam-customer-policy-blocked-kms-actions](iam-customer-policy-blocked-kms-actions.md "iam-customer-policy-blocked-kms-actions.md")                                                 | AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you<br>incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties with<br>access permissions and authorizations, restricting policies from containing<br>blocked actions on all AWS Key Management Service keys. Having more<br>privileges than needed to complete a task may violate the principle of least<br>privilege and separation of duties. This rule allows you to set the<br>blockedActionsPatterns parameter. (AWS Foundational Security Best Practices<br>value: kms:Decrypt, kms:ReEncryptFrom). The actual values should reflect<br>your organization's policies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.B   | AC-2.B Account Management                                                      | [iam-group-has-users-check](iam-group-has-users-check.md "iam-group-has-users-check.md")                                                                                           | AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) can help you<br>incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties with<br>access permissions and authorizations, by ensuring that IAM groups have at<br>least one user. Placing users in groups based on their associated<br>permissions or job function is one way to incorporate least<br>privilege.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| CCCS-fPBMM-AC-2.B   | AC-2.B Account Management                                                      | [iam-inline-policy-blocked-kms-actions](iam-inline-policy-blocked-kms-actions.md "iam-inline-policy-blocked-kms-actions.md")                                                       | Ensure an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) user,<br>IAM role or IAM group does not have an inline policy to allow blocked<br>actions on all AWS Key Management Service keys. This rule allows you to set the blockedActionsPatterns<br>parameter. (AWS Foundational Security Best Practices value: kms:Decrypt,<br>kms:ReEncryptFrom).
